questions.question: Describe the key features of the welfare state and evaluate different views on its role.

points.text: The welfare state provides NHS, education, social security, housing. Functionalists: safety net. Marxists: maintains capitalism. New Right: creates dependency. Feminists: supports women's caring role. Each perspective reveals different aspects.

questions.question: Evaluate the New Right view that welfare creates a dependency culture.

points.text: Murray: welfare removes incentive to work, creating an underclass. Evaluation: 68% of poor families have someone working (in-work poverty is the real problem); most benefit use is temporary; benefits are too low for comfortable dependency. The thesis stigmatises the poor.

questions.question: Assess whether poverty is caused by structural factors or individual behaviour.

points.text: Structural: unemployment, low wages, inadequate benefits, housing costs. Individual: laziness, poor choices (New Right). Evidence: structural factors are far more significant - most poor people are in work or seeking work. Structural solutions (living wage, affordable housing) work better.

questions.question: Full-Mark Response Evaluate the view that the welfare state has failed to reduce poverty in modern Britain. <div class="

points.text: A grade 9 response will: describe the welfare state; present evidence it HAS reduced poverty (prevents destitution, NHS improves health); present evidence it HASN'T (22% in relative poverty, in-work poverty growing); explain why: structural inequality; conclude: the welfare state has prevented absolute poverty but not eliminated relative poverty because it addresses symptoms not causes. A living wage and affordable housing would reduce poverty more effectively.
